Dearest Traveler,

Kyushu is a land born of fire, hot springs, and oceanic trade. Here, the active crater of Mount Aso smokes gently against a green caldera of breathtaking scale. In Beppu, the earth vents its steaming breath in colorful thermal pools—cobalt blues and blood reds that look like portals to another world.

But Kyushu’s warmth is not just volcanic; it is in its history of connection. In Nagasaki, the historic sea gate remained slightly open to the outer world during centuries of isolation, blending European, Chinese, and Japanese threads into a vibrant tapestry. Kyushu reminds us that our fires must burn bright, welcoming the stranger to our shore.

With volcanic passion,
Kokoro of Kyushu
